root_cause.text: The wireless extension compatibility layer fails to zero-initialize the local `struct iw_point` variable in `compat_standard_call` and `compat_private_call`, leaving its 32-bit padding hole on 64-bit architectures uninitialized and leaking kernel stack data to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds `memset(&iwp, 0, sizeof(iwp))` before copying fields to the local `struct iw_point iwp` variable in both `compat_standard_call` (in `net/wireless/wext-core.c`) and `compat_private_call` (in `net/wireless/wext-priv.c`), and the commit message states that "struct iw_point has a 32bit hole on 64bit arches" which must be zeroed to avoid disclosing 32 bits of kernel data.
